minutes.headline: Committee approved 10 school choice seats for grade 9 and 9 for grade 10, and heard the FY21 budget Q&A.
minutes.summary: The committee took public comment on Select Board remarks about the five-year plan, approved three line-item transfers, minutes and the school choice seats for next year. Most of the meeting was a budget Q&A on the superintendent's request versus the town's target, including what could be cut if the request is reduced. The timeline for budget presentation to the Finance Committee was discussed, and the committee went into executive session for collective bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Member-style comment criticizing Select Board behavior and overreach in discussing the school five-year plan.
Shared frustration over Select Board discussions; urged strategic conversation on debt service, capital and programs.
Asked whether the town manager's 2.5 percent projection has flexibility versus the 4 percent proposal.
Asked whether reducing staff to part-time risks losing good people.
Resident thanked the committee, said the 4 percent budget is critical need with no fudge.
Resident urged continued advocacy, attending Select Board and Finance meetings, and parent mobilization; shared personal story on primary school services.
Resident asked how to handle school questions at Select Board meetings when no school representative is present.
Resident reported on a safety conference, urged unity among parents and departments over funding, and praised teachers and middle school program.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to approve school choice seats for grades 9 and 10 for next year, with the application to post the next day.
Most of the meeting was a Q&A on the FY21 budget: the superintendent's request is higher than the town's target, and figures are still shifting.
The committee discussed moving its first March meeting to March 11 for budget review, a further Q&A on March 18, and the budget hearing and vote in April.
The committee moved to accept three line-item transfers; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
Public comment early in the meeting concerned Select Board remarks on the school five-year plan, and the committee closed in executive session on collective bargaining.

why_it_matters: The school request and the town's target for FY21 have not been reconciled, so what the schools can fund, and what Town Meeting is asked to vote on in the spring, depends on figures still changing, including state aid, new growth and health insurance.
School choice seats set how many students from outside the district can enroll in the high school grades, which affects class size and the district's funding from tuition.
watch_next: Possible March 11 and March 18 budget meetings, then the budget hearing and vote in April.
Final health insurance figures, due at the end of the month.
